correctness.rationale: Independent replay: python /workspace/review-evidence/3.py. It reconstructs GP(10,2), enumerates every simple cycle via its least edge, verifies girth 5 and 1,168 cycles, and enumerates all relevant vertex-disjoint triples: no cycle over length 10 fits alongside two cycles of length at least 5. The 56 triples split 20/30/6 at maxima 5/8/10. Using a different vertex numbering, consecutive reduced half-edge differences, and signed exterior products, the replay gives 9,120 top chains, 22,800 degree-two chains, 56 zero integer boundaries, binary differential rank 9,094, and unit minors (-1,+1) for the 20 and 26 chosen chains. This gives a rational kernel of dimension 26, and the full unit minor gives an integral coordinate retraction: no finite index remains. Every octagon chain matches a signed pair of distinct pentagon chains in all coordinates; independently, each octagon is the outer boundary of two pentagons sharing an edge, with no new vertices, so this relation is compatible with the other two disjoint cycles. The first 20 elements of the basis span a primitive lattice, leaving a free rank-six quotient. The exhaustive maximum-length list rules out generation at nine as well as eight. The weight-three reduced comparison theorem, its natural embedding maps, and its tensor product on disjoint subgraphs identify the signed cycle products with actual geometric tori of the unordered space, not merely cycles in an arbitrary chain complex. The frozen verifier and output were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral graph and its face loops give a natural geometric filtration of a known configuration-space group. Knowing that face tori already span a primitive rank-20 subgroup, that all allowable octagons add nothing, and that six specific ten-cycle tori supply exactly the missing primitive generators distinguishes geometry and integral structure invisible to the known Betti number. This is an exact usable basis and cutoff, not a repeat of the rank calculation.
